components.name: Laptop
components.description: CC0 low-poly laptop drawn with three.js (laptop3d.js), lid hinged in code, the real #screen link on its glass via CSS3DRenderer. Page 100 shows me as rotating ASCII (head-ascii.js); other pages show their screenshot as 8-colour block mosaic. Scrolling flies it (shut, one spin, cyan/magenta ghosts) onto the ASCII table, where the guide draws in.

components.name: Scroll Hint
components.description: Fixed bottom-right red block "▼ SCROLL DOWN ▼", flashing red/yellow, arrows hopping; hidden once you scroll.

narrative.overview: The home page (`index.html`) is a broadcast teletext service called BPTEXT. Everything sits on flat black glass in the eight broadcast colours, set in one blocky character-cell face (Bedstead, the public-domain SAA5050 lookalike). Every page of the site has a three-digit number (100 me, 200 Resume, 300 How this site runs, 400 About, 500 Projects, 600 Other work). The centrepiece is a chunky 3D laptop beside the name: its screen shows me as rotating ASCII (page 100) or another page's screenshot redrawn as 8-colour block mosaic, the coloured Fastext keys change what's on it, and clicking the screen opens that page through TV static that clears into focus. Scrolling down, the laptop shuts, spins once and lands on an ASCII-drawn table, where a guide to the page on its screen draws in beside it.
keyCharacteristics: Black ground, the broadcast eight only, each colour with one job.
One face, one weight (Bedstead 400); hierarchy by colour and double height, never by weight.
Hard 2px boxes and bands; zero radius anywhere.
Every section is a three-digit page with a coloured double-height title band.
Stepped motion: row-by-row draw, a jittering page counter, a blinking LED. The one exception is the user-approved opening, where grey static fades and the page eases from blur into focus.

rules.name: The Broadcast Eight Rule
rules.body: No colour outside the eight, no tints, no opacity mixes on text. The block-mosaic previews quantise to the same eight values (`PALETTE` in `home-teletext.js`).

rules.name: The Black Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on any filled colour is black, except on Navigation Blue, where it is white (`--band-ink:#fff`).

rules.name: The Double Height Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is teletext double height: the same glyphs stretched with `transform: scaleY(2)` from the top, with padding-bottom reserving the space the transform does not take. Used on the header row, the name, title bands and project titles. Never bold, never a second face.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Bedstead at 400 only; `<b>` inside the feature panel is the single exception and renders as the face allows.

rules.name: The Glass Rule
rules.body: The only overlay is the screen's scan lines: a fixed repeating band of 1px at 22% black every 3px. No other gradient, glow or blur appears at rest.

dos: **Do** give every new home section a three-digit page number, a `data-page`, a double-height title band in one of the eight colours, and an entry in the PAGES list.
**Do** keep text black on filled colour and white only on Navigation Blue.
**Do** express hover and pressed states as an instant fill with the element's own colour, never a fade.
**Do** keep motion stepped (`steps()`, row-by-row, blink); eased motion belongs only to the tune-in opening.
**Do** measure inline spacing in `ch` and keep every box square-cornered with 2px borders.
donts: **Don't** introduce a colour outside the broadcast eight, or tints and opacity on text.
**Don't** use a second typeface or a bold weight for hierarchy; use colour and double height.
**Don't** add border radius, drop shadows, glows or gradient fills; the scan-line overlay is the only texture.
**Don't** carry this world onto another page or pull the CRT, C64-blue or lab tokens into it; each page keeps its own world.
